standard.description: Light measurement (A2LA scope CMC, radiometer standards)
standard.confidence_text: approximately the 95 % level, usually k = 2 (A2LA scope, footnote 2)
standard.reference: Calibration Scope of Accreditation, A2LA 1888.03, rev. 07/07/2026, printed p. 45 of 47, section X. Optical Quantities (Light - Measure)
standard.author: written by specs/build_light_standard.py from the scope text

notes.1: SOURCE: the laboratory's own A2LA scope of accreditation, certificate 1888.03 (revised 07/07/2026), printed p. 45 of 47, section X. Optical Quantities, parameter "Light - Measure": White (0 to 3000) FC, (0 to 35 000) lux, (0 to 100 000) La, each CMC 2.9 %; Black @ 365 nm (0 to 3000) uW/cm2, CMC 5.0 %. Comments: "Radiometer standards." Page 45 of 47 is the scope's own page numbering. Built by specs/build_light_standard.py.
notes.2: VERIFICATION: the Light row (column header CMC 2, 5, 12 (+/-), four ranges, 2.9 % / 2.9 % / 2.9 % / 5.0 %, units FC, lux, La, micro-W/cm2) was read from the RENDERED PAGE IMAGE of p. 45 of 47 (cert. 1888.03, revised 07/07/2026) on 2026-10-23.
notes.3: CONFIDENCE: footnote 2 of the scope: the CMC is the smallest uncertainty the laboratory can achieve, an EXPANDED uncertainty at approximately the 95 % level, usually k = 2. Stored as confidence_pct 95, so the coverage divisor is 2.0 (u of the standard = CMC / 2). Wording kept in confidence_text.
notes.4: PERCENTAGE: footnote 5 of the scope: the first percentage is a percentage of the READING unless otherwise noted. Each row is +/-(CMC % I.V.) with no fixed term and no full-scale term, so the uncertainty is CMC x |reading| (2.9 % of 10 000 lux = 290 lux). The figure is not a floor-limited value: nothing is added at the bottom of a range.
notes.5: INSTRUMENT TYPE: footnote 12 of the scope: the parameter defines the type of instrument calibrated (light meters / radiometers). The scope comment is "Radiometer standards": the laboratory's reference is a radiometer-based standard, so this CMC is the uncertainty of the lab's standard for the light level it applies to the unit under test.
notes.6: UNITS (as listed on the scope, each its own unit, nothing converted): FC, lux, La, uW/cm2 (printed with the micro sign and a superscript 2; the stored unit is ASCII "uW/cm2"). For information only, never used in a calculation: 1 FC = 10.763910416709722 lux (lux is the SI unit of illuminance); 1 La = 10000/pi cd/m2 (a luminance unit, not an illuminance). The three white-light rows are the same CMC (2.9 %) on three different scales, so a lux value is never looked up in the FC or La rows.
notes.7: DIRECTION AND PERIOD: the scope parameter is "Measure"; the sheet stores direction "output" (the light level the lab's standard establishes at the unit under test), which is what the default lookup (specmanager, tartur.standard_accuracy) asks for. A CMC has no 90 day / 1 yr column: it is stored once, under the period "1 yr" (the default period of every standard).
notes.8: NOT STORED: stability, non-uniformity, spectral mismatch or distance-dependent terms of the radiometer standard, and the unit under test (resolution, repeatability, drift). The CMC excludes the unit under test; a certificate value may be larger. No other wavelength, no spectral irradiance and no radiometric unit other than uW/cm2 at 365 nm is on the scope.

limits.limit: FC 0 to 3000; lux 0 to 35 000; La 0 to 100 000; CMC 2.9 % of reading on each scale.
0 to 3000 uW/cm2 at 365 nm; CMC 5.0 % of reading.

problems.what: This is the laboratory's own CMC (expanded, approximately 95 %, usually k = 2), not a manufacturer specification. No fixed term and no period columns; stored under the period "1 yr".
FC and La are not SI illuminance units; they are kept as the scope lists them and not converted to lux (the CMC is a percentage, so no conversion is needed).
